quests.instruction: From her bedroom window, Mina sees a bright flash in the sky and, a few seconds later, hears a deep rumble.
quests.question: What is the bright flash?
options: Hail
Lightning
Thunder
A rainbow
quests.correctAnswer: Lightning
quests.hint: One of these you see and the other you hear.
quests.explanation: The bright flash is lightning, which is a giant spark of electricity. The rumble that follows is thunder.
quests.funFact: A lightning bolt can be several times hotter than the surface of the Sun.

quests.instruction: A teacher asks the class what makes the booming sound of thunder.
quests.question: What causes thunder?
options: Lightning heats air that suddenly expands
Wind whistling through narrow canyons
Raindrops hitting the ground very hard
Clouds crashing into each other overhead
quests.correctAnswer: Lightning heats air that suddenly expands
quests.hint: Imagine what lightning does to the air around it.
quests.explanation: Lightning heats the air around it in a split second, and the air bursts outward, creating a shock of sound.
quests.funFact: Thunder can sometimes be heard from ten kilometres away or more.

quests.instruction: Dark skies are gathering and Ravi wants to know which cloud usually brings thunderstorms.
quests.question: Which cloud is it?
options: A small, puffy white cloud
A low, flat grey sheet
A tall, dark, towering cloud
A thin, wispy cloud
quests.correctAnswer: A tall, dark, towering cloud
quests.hint: Thunderstorms need clouds with a lot of height and energy.
quests.explanation: Thunderstorms grow in tall clouds that rise high into the sky. Thin or small clouds don't have enough power.
quests.funFact: Some thunderclouds are taller than Mount Everest.

quests.instruction: At the lake, Kiran notices she always sees lightning first and hears thunder afterwards.
quests.question: Why does the sound come later?
options: Thunder happens before lightning
The lightning is closer to her
Light travels much faster than sound
Her ears are slow
quests.correctAnswer: Light travels much faster than sound
quests.hint: Focus on which one wins a race.
quests.explanation: Light moves nearly a million times faster than sound, so you see the flash almost instantly but hear the thunder later.
quests.funFact: Light travels nearly a million times faster than sound.

quests.instruction: Two storms flash at the same moment. At storm A the thunder arrives 2 seconds later, and at storm B it arrives 10 seconds later.
quests.question: Which storm is closer?
options: Storm B
They are the same distance
It depends on the colour of the flash
Storm A
quests.correctAnswer: Storm A
quests.hint: Sound needs time to travel, so a shorter wait means a shorter distance.
quests.explanation: The shorter the gap between flash and thunder, the less distance the sound had to travel.
quests.funFact: Sound travels about one kilometre in three seconds.

quests.instruction: Lena counts six seconds between a lightning flash and the thunder. She remembers that sound takes about three seconds to travel a kilometre.
quests.question: About how far away was the lightning?
options: About 20 kilometres
About 200 metres
About 6 kilometres
About 2 kilometres
quests.correctAnswer: About 2 kilometres
quests.hint: Divide the seconds by the number of seconds per kilometre.
quests.explanation: Six seconds divided by three seconds per kilometre gives about 2 kilometres.
quests.funFact: In miles, you can count about five seconds for each mile.

quests.instruction: The class is playing in the park when Omar hears a clap of thunder in the distance.
quests.question: What should they do?
options: Stand under a tree
Go indoors right away
Wait to see a flash first
Finish the game quickly
quests.correctAnswer: Go indoors right away
quests.hint: If you can hear the storm, it is already close enough to matter.
quests.explanation: Thunder means lightning is near, so going indoors straight away is the safest choice.
quests.funFact: A popular saying goes: when thunder roars, go indoors.

quests.instruction: Parents talk about safe places to wait out a lightning storm.
quests.question: Where should the family wait out the lightning?
options: Under the branches of a tall tree
In the middle of an open field
On the very top of a hill
Inside a closed building or car
quests.correctAnswer: Inside a closed building or car
quests.hint: Remember being surrounded by solid walls or metal.
quests.explanation: A building or a car with a metal roof helps guide lightning around you, so you stay safer inside.
quests.funFact: Tall trees, towers and hills are common targets for lightning.

quests.instruction: A hiker says she wants to shelter under a tall tree during a thunderstorm.
quests.question: Why is that dangerous?
options: Trees make the thunder sound louder
Lightning tends to hit tall things
Trees attract extra rain from clouds
Leaves fall faster in heavy rain
quests.correctAnswer: Lightning tends to hit tall things
quests.hint: Notice which object sticks up the most.
quests.explanation: Lightning tends to hit tall things, and a tree can pass electricity along to people standing under it.
quests.funFact: Trees struck by lightning can lose their bark in strips.

quests.instruction: Children are swimming in a pool when they hear thunder.
quests.question: What should they do?
options: Get out of the water and go inside
Swim to the middle of the pool
Stay in but finish quickly
Dive to the bottom of the pool
quests.correctAnswer: Get out of the water and go inside
quests.hint: Water and electricity are a risky pair.
quests.explanation: Water can carry electricity, so leaving the pool and going indoors is safest.
quests.funFact: Lightning can strike the water and spread through it.

quests.instruction: A storm is rumbling overhead while the family stays at home.
quests.question: Which activity is best avoided indoors?
options: Drawing at the table
Taking a bath or shower
Playing a board game
Reading a book
quests.correctAnswer: Taking a bath or shower
quests.hint: Consider what connects to the outside of the house.
quests.explanation: Lightning's electricity can travel through plumbing, so it's wise to wait until the storm passes.
quests.funFact: Lightning current can also travel through wiring.

quests.instruction: The thunder has stopped and the rain is easing. Ana's friends want to run outside.
quests.question: When is it sensible to go back out?
options: When the clouds start looking white
As soon as the rain begins to slow
After about one minute of quiet
About 30 minutes after the last thunder
quests.correctAnswer: About 30 minutes after the last thunder
quests.hint: A storm can linger after the rain begins to fade.
quests.explanation: Lightning can still strike from the edge of a storm, so waiting about 30 minutes after the last thunder is safer.
quests.funFact: Lightning can strike several kilometres away from the heart of a storm.

quests.instruction: Suddenly the air turns cooler, a gust of wind blows, and tall dark clouds appear.
quests.question: What do these clues suggest?
options: Thick fog is starting to form
Snow is just about to fall
A long heat wave is starting
A storm may be on its way
quests.correctAnswer: A storm may be on its way
quests.hint: Put together all the clues: wind, temperature and clouds.
quests.explanation: A cool gust and towering dark clouds are typical signs that a thunderstorm is close.
quests.funFact: The cool gust before a storm is cold air rushing out of the storm cloud.

quests.instruction: Dev is under a blue sky when he hears distant thunder.
quests.question: What does this tell him?
options: A storm may be near, even if not overhead
There is no storm anywhere nearby
It must be noise from far-away traffic
Thunder can't travel very far at all
quests.correctAnswer: A storm may be near, even if not overhead
quests.hint: Picture how far sound can travel.
quests.explanation: Thunder can be heard from far away, which means a storm is near enough to take seriously.
quests.funFact: Lightning can strike a long way from the storm cloud that made it.

quests.instruction: A group counts the gap between each flash and its thunder. The gap keeps getting longer.
quests.question: What is the storm doing?
options: Moving closer
Getting weaker for sure
Moving away
Standing still
quests.correctAnswer: Moving away
quests.hint: Longer gaps mean the sound has farther to travel.
quests.explanation: A growing gap between flash and thunder shows the storm is moving farther away.
quests.funFact: Many thunderstorms travel at about the speed of a car in town.

quests.instruction: Ria's science teacher asks the class what lightning really is.
quests.question: What is lightning?
options: A huge electric spark in the sky
A flash of light made by the Moon
A burst of cold wind high up
A beam of sunlight through clouds
quests.correctAnswer: A huge electric spark in the sky
quests.hint: Think of a huge version of something you can create with a balloon.
quests.explanation: Lightning is a giant electric spark that jumps between clouds or between a cloud and the ground.
quests.funFact: A typical lightning flash lasts less than a second.

quests.instruction: Nina feels a tiny spark when she touches a metal door handle after walking on the carpet.
quests.question: Which part of weather is this like?
options: A tiny version of heavy rain
A tiny version of lightning
A tiny version of thick fog
A tiny version of hailstones
quests.correctAnswer: A tiny version of lightning
quests.hint: Both involve electric charge jumping across a gap.
quests.explanation: Static electricity builds up and jumps as a small spark, which is similar to lightning but much weaker.
quests.funFact: Ice particles rubbing together inside storm clouds help build up electric charge.

quests.instruction: On a hot, sticky afternoon, Arun notices big clouds building up quickly.
quests.question: Why do storms often build on hot, humid afternoons?
options: Warm, moist air rises and forms tall clouds
Cold air sinks and spreads over the ground
The wind drops and the air goes still
Cold sea water rises into the air
quests.correctAnswer: Warm, moist air rises and forms tall clouds
quests.hint: Imagine what warm, damp air does.
quests.explanation: Hot, moist air rises quickly, cools and forms tall clouds that can turn into thunderstorms.
quests.funFact: In many tropical places, afternoon thunderstorms happen almost every day in the rainy season.

quests.instruction: A very tall building has a metal rod on its roof.
quests.question: What is the rod for?
options: To attract rain to the building
To measure how fast the wind blows
To guide lightning safely down
To hold up a flag on the roof
quests.correctAnswer: To guide lightning safely down
quests.hint: Focus on giving electricity an easy path.
quests.explanation: A lightning rod gives lightning a safe path to the ground so it doesn't damage the building.
quests.funFact: Benjamin Franklin is credited with developing the lightning rod in the 1750s.

quests.instruction: A loud, sharp crack of thunder follows almost instantly after a flash.
quests.question: What does the sharp crack tell you?
options: The storm is ending
The lightning was very close
The rain has stopped
The lightning was far away
quests.correctAnswer: The lightning was very close
quests.hint: A short gap means sound had little distance to travel.
quests.explanation: A sharp crack right after a flash means the lightning struck nearby.
quests.funFact: Distant thunder rumbles because sound reaches you from different parts of the bolt at different times.

quests.instruction: During a summer storm, hard balls of ice bounce on the road.
quests.question: What are they?
options: Frost
Drizzle
Hail
Snow
quests.correctAnswer: Hail
quests.hint: These balls of ice come from the same storm clouds as thunder.
quests.explanation: Hail forms in tall storm clouds where updrafts toss ice up and down so it grows in layers.
quests.funFact: Hailstones can sometimes grow as big as golf balls.

quests.instruction: Sam counts nine seconds between flash and thunder, and a few minutes later counts only four seconds.
quests.question: What is happening to the storm?
options: It has disappeared
It is moving away
It has stopped moving
It is getting closer
quests.correctAnswer: It is getting closer
quests.hint: Compare the two gaps.
quests.explanation: A shrinking gap means thunder is arriving sooner, so the storm is getting closer.
quests.funFact: At any moment, there are thousands of thunderstorms happening somewhere on Earth.

quests.instruction: A child is cycling across an open field when thunder rumbles overhead.
quests.question: What is the safest move?
options: Hide under a lone tree
Lie flat in the middle of the field
Pedal faster across the field
Leave the bike and go inside a building
quests.correctAnswer: Leave the bike and go inside a building
quests.hint: In open ground, a person can be the tallest thing around.
quests.explanation: Open fields are risky because a person may be the tallest object. Getting into a building is safest.
quests.funFact: People standing alone in open spaces are more at risk because they are tall relative to the ground.

quests.instruction: A student claims that lightning never strikes the same place twice.
quests.question: Which statement about lightning is a myth?
options: Lightning is a powerful form of electricity
Lightning often strikes tall objects
Lightning never hits the same place twice
Lightning is much hotter than a flame
quests.correctAnswer: Lightning never hits the same place twice
quests.hint: Remember tall buildings that get hit often.
quests.explanation: Lightning often strikes the same tall places again and again.
quests.funFact: The Empire State Building is struck by lightning about 20 to 25 times a year.

quests.instruction: A thunderstorm warning has been announced for this evening, and the school has an outdoor concert planned.
quests.question: What is the best plan?
options: Move it under the trees
Keep it outside as planned
Move it indoors or reschedule
Go ahead with a shorter show
quests.correctAnswer: Move it indoors or reschedule
quests.hint: Notice the safest place for a crowd.
quests.explanation: Large outdoor events are risky in thunderstorms. Moving indoors or choosing another time keeps people safe.
quests.funFact: Many sports games are paused during lightning and restart when it has passed.

quests.instruction: Parents say it's a good idea to unplug the television and computer when a thunderstorm is overhead.
quests.question: Why would they do that?
options: Lightning can cause a surge in the wires
Thunder makes the sets far too noisy
Wind could switch the sets off for good
Rain would make the sets wet inside
quests.correctAnswer: Lightning can cause a surge in the wires
quests.hint: Consider what lightning can do to wires.
quests.explanation: A strike near power lines can send a sudden surge into the house, which can damage devices.
quests.funFact: A surge protector can reduce the risk but doesn't make lightning harmless.

quests.instruction: At midday during a heavy storm, the sky is as dark as dusk.
quests.question: Why is it so dark in the middle of the day?
options: Thick, tall clouds block the sunlight
The thunder makes the sky go dark
The Sun has gone down much too early
The Moon is covering the Sun
quests.correctAnswer: Thick, tall clouds block the sunlight
quests.hint: What is between you and the Sun?
quests.explanation: Storm clouds are thick and tall, so they block most sunlight and make the day look dark.
quests.funFact: Tall storm clouds can make midday look like dusk.

quests.instruction: Aarav counts twelve seconds between a flash and a low rumble, and the sky ahead looks dark.
quests.question: What should he decide?
options: The storm has already gone far away
It is just a loud truck passing by
It is safe to stay out all afternoon
Go inside soon; it's a few km away
quests.correctAnswer: Go inside soon; it's a few km away
quests.hint: Use the counting rule from earlier.
quests.explanation: Twelve seconds is about four kilometres, which is close enough to head indoors.
quests.funFact: Lightning flashes about 40 times every second around the world.

quests.instruction: A class works out a safety plan for when thunder is heard.
quests.question: Which pair of actions is the best?
options: Swim underwater and hold the railing
Go indoors and stay away from water
Stand in the open and call a friend
Wait beneath a tree
quests.correctAnswer: Go indoors and stay away from water
quests.hint: Picture both height and water.
quests.explanation: Going indoors and keeping away from water protects you from the two biggest risks.
quests.funFact: Plumbing and pools can both carry electricity from lightning.

quests.instruction: Priya's little brother is scared of thunder.
quests.question: Which explanation is both true and calming?
options: Thunder is lightning's sound, and indoors is safe
Thunder is the Sun being very loud up high
Thunder is rain falling on the sky itself
Thunder is clouds crashing, and it can't be stopped
quests.correctAnswer: Thunder is lightning's sound, and indoors is safe
quests.hint: Give the cause first, then the safe thing to do.
quests.explanation: Thunder is only a sound, and staying inside during a storm keeps us safe from lightning.
quests.funFact: Thunder can't hurt you; the danger comes from the lightning that makes it.
